guidance.heading: Outlook for 2026 and 2027
section: DTE Energy confirms 2026 operating EPS guidance of $7.59 to $7.73. DTE Energy also provided a 2027 operating EPS pro forma baseline2 range of $7.59 - $7.73, which reflects the DTE Vantage asset sale.

“Strong financial performance through the third quarter of 2026 positions us to continue investing in Michigan’s energy infrastructure while delivering long-term value for our customers, communities and shareholders,” said David Ruud, DTE vice chairman and CFO.
Advisors to DTE Vantage Transaction Lazard is acting as exclusive financial advisor to DTE Energy, and Kirkland & Ellis LLP is acting as legal advisor to DTE Energy.

Footnote (1): Includes the sale of primarily all DTE Vantage assets, except EES Coke Footnote (2): Reflective of closing the Vantage transaction by year-end 2026 and is subject to change based on impacts from discontinued operations, actual closing timing and the timing of deployment of sale proceeds
This earnings announcement and presentation slides are available at dteenergy.com/investors.

The company will conduct a conference call to discuss earnings results at 9:00 a.m. ET. desk.headline: Operating EPS $2.30 vs $2.25 a year ago, beat; 2026 guidance confirmed, $3bn Vantage sale and a flat 2027 baseline of $7.59–7.73
results: Operating EPS rose to $2.30 from $2.25 (GAAP $2.25 vs $2.01); operating earnings were $481m.
DTE Electric earned less ($468m vs $541m) on tax timing, a bigger asset base and storm costs, partly offset by new rates and warm weather.
The non-utility Vantage unit more than doubled to $110m on higher renewable gas output and tax credits — the business now being sold.
Agreed to sell DTE Vantage for about $3bn to investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management; closing expected in the first half of 2027.
Michigan regulators approved the Google data centre contracts, taking signed data centre load to 2.4 GW.

guidance.summary: 2026 operating EPS guidance of $7.59–7.73 confirmed, with the company saying it is heading for the high end. A new 2027 'pro forma baseline' at the same $7.59–7.73 reflects the earnings lost with Vantage; the long-term growth target is above 9% a year through 2031.

points: CEO Joi Harris framed the Vantage sale as sharpening focus on the regulated utilities, turning DTE into a faster-growing utility after 2027.
Data centres are central: 2.4 GW signed (Oracle 1.4 GW, Google 1 GW), about 2 GW in advanced talks and another deal targeted by end-2026.
Management argued data centre load spreads fixed costs and helps existing customers' bills; the Oracle ramp could let DTE delay its next electric rate case to at least 2028.
Equity needs rise to about $1bn a year over 2027–2031 to fund the bigger plan; $500m of 2026 forward equity is pushed into 2027.
Coverage notes the 2027 baseline is flat with 2026 and that the old earnings path is not expected to be regained until around 2029.
call.source: Call coverage: Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 5 Nov 2026; Utility Dive, 6 Nov 2026; earnings slides (Exhibit 99.2)

watch: Whether a third data centre agreement is signed by year-end.
Regulatory approval and timing of the Vantage sale (the 2027 baseline assumes an earlier close than the first-half 2027 target).
The electric rate case order due around February 2027 and the large-load tariff.
